\begin{example} \end{example}[$\varepsilon $-dense finite approximation]

Source: petersen:page-0410, petersen:page-0411 ↗ def:pet-ch11-gromov-hausdorff-distance ↗ def:pet-ch11-hausdorff-distance 1. ch11:11.1.4For compact $X$ and finite $A\subset X$ with $d_H(A,X)\le \varepsilon $ (using the induced metric on $A$), call $A$ $\varepsilon $-dense in $X$. Then $\dGH (X,A)\le \varepsilon $; since $X$ is compact, finite $\varepsilon $-dense subsets exist for every $\varepsilon >0$. \end{example}
Proof

↗ ex:pet-ch11-epsilon-dense-approximation \sketch For $\delta >0$, define the cross-distance on $X\sqcup A$ by $|xa|=\delta +|xa|_X$. This admissible metric has $d_H(X,A)<\varepsilon +\delta $; let $\delta \downarrow 0$.
